claims.claim: The work is attributed to Hesychius, a priest of Jerusalem (πρεσβύτερος Ἱεροσολύμων).
The author states he found the martyrdom account of Saint Longinus in a manuscript in the library of the Holy Sepulchre (τῇ βιβλιοθήκῃ τῆς ἁγίας Ἀναστάσεως) after much searching and labor.
The work was composed to present the martyrdom and encomium of Saint Longinus the centurion, who confessed Christ at the crucifixion, so that believers might be confirmed in faith.
The work concerns the legend of Longinus, the centurion who attended the crucifixion and believed in Christ (Matt. 27:54; Mark 15:39), preached Christianity in Cappadocia, and died a martyr.
The work survives in an abridged form in tenth-century Synaxaria.
The work is transmitted in Patrologia Graeca 93, columns 1545–1560, under the title 'Martyrium sancti Longini centurionis'.
The work was edited by M. Aubineau in 'Les homélies festales d'Hésychius de Jérusalem, Vol. 2. Les homélies xvi-xxi' (Subsidia hagiographica 59), Brussels, 1980, pages 817–844.
The attribution to the fifth-century Hesychius of Jerusalem is disputed; the work is marked as '[Dub.]' (dubious) and the author is identified as 'not the fifth-century writer'.
The work is classified as BHG 0988z in the Bibliotheca Hagiographica Graeca.
